overview: Virtualize two axes with stable IDs and bounded overscan; offscreen data and selected IDs are independent of DOM rows. Server sorts/filters the entire dataset. A worker can format/index only loaded data; it cannot make sorting one cached page equivalent to sorting all rows. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.result: Window both dimensions; keep the focused cell mounted or move focus deliberately
estimation.implication: Profile scroll/resize and worker messaging, measure memory for retained pages separately.

components.purpose: Virtualize two axes with stable IDs and bounded overscan; offscreen data and selected IDs are independent of DOM rows. Server sorts/filters the entire dataset. A worker can format/index only loaded data; it cannot make sorting one cached page equivalent to sorting all rows. Performance plan: 100,000 × 50 cells; target around 40 mounted rows and 12 mounted columns including overscan. Accessibility: Use table semantics for read-only data; interactive grid needs roving tabIndex, arrow/Home/End navigation, correct logical row/column indices and a focused-cell strategy across virtualization. Failure recovery: Send expected row version; on 409 preserve the draft, show current value and ask how to resolve. Cancel stale query responses on sorting changes. Trade-off: Simple server-paginated tables are cheaper and often more accessible. Full grid behavior is justified by editing and spreadsheet-like navigation.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
